newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said 24 percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was harvested compared with 38 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 35 percent.

In the report on conditions for the week ended June 29, USDA said two percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in very poor condition, eight percent poor, 25 percent fair, 52 percent good and 13 percent excellent.
The department said one percent of the U.S. corn crop was in very poor condition, four percent poor, 21 percent fair, 57 percent good and 17 percent excellent.
The department said three percent of the U.S. corn crop was silking, compared with four percent a year ago and four percent for the five year average.
It said one percent of the U.S. soybean crop was in very poor condition, six percent poor, 28 percent fair, 54 percent good and 11 percent excellent.
The USDA said three percent of the soybean crop was blooming, compared with three percent one year ago and the five-year average of four percent.
The department reported three percent of the U.S. cotton crop was in very poor condition, 10 percent poor, 31 percent fair, 45 percent good and 11 percent excellent.
USDA said three percent of the U.S. spring wheat crop was in very poor condition, 14 percent poor, 33 percent fair, 44 percent good and six percent excellent.
